body.spec_md: qualifier/Q1/plain-amount.ts exports plainAmount(value, decimals, symbol) -> string. value is an integer number of base units as a string, which may start with a minus sign and may use Arabic Indic digits. The result uses Latin digits, groups thousands with commas, keeps at least 2 and at most decimals decimals (zeros beyond 2 removed from the end), writes a negative value as "minus 1,234.50 USDC" and never contains a dash. Invalid input throws.

body.notes: Q1: plainAmount formats an integer base-unit string without floating point: digits are normalised from Arabic-Indic to Latin, grouping is applied to the integer part only, the fraction keeps at least 2 and at most `decimals` digits with trailing zeros beyond 2 removed, a negative value is written with the word `minus ` and never with a dash, and negative zero is zero. Invalid shapes throw instead of guessing. Nine tests, each named after the acceptance item. Every test name carries its acceptance item, and the suite runs with no install on Node 24.

note: Captured with one real paid call from the agent's own wallet. The payTo is the same fleet wallet, so the 0.005 USDC transfer is to itself (net zero); the point is that the endpoint answered after a verified and settled x402 payment.
